full_judgment: 4. Ms. Nihad Kabir, the learned Advocate, has appeared in Reference Application Nos. 16/93 and 17/93 for the Applicant and in Reference Application No. 48/95 for the Respondent. She supports the decision of the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, given in I.T.A. NI. 2109 of 1991-92, but questions the legality of its decision given in I.T.A. No. 2293 and 2244 of 1987-88. She submits that the Tribunal erroneously held in I.T.A. Nos. 2293 and 2244 of 1987-88 the status of the company to be resident and ordinarily resident in the country, despite the fact that the company was a public limited company registered in the United Kingdom with its Head Office in Glasgow. She submits that the company is controlled from the united Kindom where all of its di-rectors reside and all the policy decisions regarding the affairs of the company is taken. She submits that the status of the company is to be determined by referring to the provisions or section 4(1)(3) of the convention, read with section 4(A)(C) of the income Tax Act, 1922 and section 2(55)(c) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984. The learned Advocate submits that the Tribunal erred in law in proceeding with the presumption that the company was resident in both U.K. and Bangladesh on the ground that the executives of the assessee effectively manage it business and for this purpose power has been delegated to them by the Head Office in the U.K. but this finding is based on pure surmise and conjecture. The Tribunal erred in holding that the company has resident status in Bangladesh taking the view that its effective management is in the hands of the executives in Bangladesh so far its Bangladesh business is concerned.
